BOARD RESPONSIBILITY STATEMENT
Recognising our responsibility to stakeholders, the senior leadership of Godrej Properties Limited is committed to 
presenting a transparent and comprehensive integrated report. We believe this report thoroughly addresses all material matters that could impact our ability to create sustainable value.The content index can be accessed at Pg. 520
The fourth Annual Integrated Report of Godrej Properties Limited offers a comprehensive view of our financial, operational, and sustainability performance for the year. It showcases how we are creating value across short, medium, and long-term horizons, while balancing business growth with our commitment to responsible development. Through integrated thinking and transparent disclosures, the report provides stakeholders with deeper insights into our strategy, governance, and progress towards building resilient, future-ready communities.ABOUT THE REPORT

The accuracy of the data and processes presented in our report has been assured by TUV SUD South Asia Pvt. Ltd., an independent third-party assurance provider. SCOPE OF THE REPORT
The scope of this Report includes the strategic narrative and focuses on our ongoing project sites in India, developed either directly or through our special purpose vehicles. Unless stated otherwise, information and content have been consolidated for the purpose of reporting.
Where relevant, the report also extends its 
boundary to include key risks and opportunities arising from entities and stakeholders that affect our ability to create value. These entities and stakeholders may not be under our direct control or influence, but play a critical role in our value creation journey due to the nature and proximity of their impact. This report details our environmental performance across 63 active project sites, and 8 offices, including our headquarters in Mumbai, which are under our direct operational control.

GODREJ INDUSTRIES GROUP
At the Godrej Industries Group (GIG), we are committed to growing and strengthening 
this legacy. We are privileged to serve over 1.1 billion consumers globally through our businesses with market leadership positions in the consumer products, real estate, agriculture, financial services and chemicals industries.
their portfolio businesses, including 
the leading producers of compound feed and crude palm oil, address key challenges faced by Indian agriculture; and help improve productivity of Indian farmers through innovative products and services that sustainably increase crop and livestock yields. is an emerging markets FMCG leader in Home and Personal Care with a growing presence in Asia, Africa and Latin America.is the real estate private equity arm of the group.
is group’s oldest business, services diverse industrial applications through one of India’s oldest and largest oleo-chemicals, derivatives and speciality chemical portfolios.is India’s leading real estate developer by sales and brings the Godrej philosophy of innovation, sustainability, and excellence to the real estate industry.is the newest company in the group, has a fast-growing financial services business.
BUILDING ON  
128 YEARS  
OF TRUSTGodrej was founded in 1897 by Ardeshir Godrej to help build economic independence for India. We contributed to this purpose by both innovating and actively donating a significant portion of the Group’s profits to India’s freedom movement. 
During the Spanish Flu pandemic of 1918, we 
pioneered the world’s first commercially made soap from vegetable oil, free of animal fat. In 1951, we crafted the ballot boxes for free India’s first general election, where every citizen, regardless of gender, had the right to vote.
This legacy of nation-building continues to guide 
our actions today. As we expand our footprint, we are equally focused on driving positive impact - by integrating sustainability and inclusion into everything we do. 
Through Godrej Good & Green, we align with 
global goals and local community needs to enable a greener, more equitable world. And through the Godrej DEI Lab, we are building inclusive ecosystems, nurturing diverse talent, and bringing DEI-driven innovation to the fore.

Dear Shareholders, 
I hope this message finds you and your loved 
ones well.
FY 2024–25 was a landmark year for Godrej 
Properties—one where we saw the rewards of focused execution, customer-centricity, and long-term thinking come together. As India continues to lead global economic growth and urban transformation, the real estate sector has played a vital role in driving opportunity, progress, and impact.
At Godrej Properties, we remain guided by 
our core purpose: to create spaces that enable Everyday Joys: one home, one community, one city at a time. The year gone by saw us deepen our presence across key markets, introduce exceptional new projects, and embed sustainability and inclusion even more firmly into our operations. It was also a year where we further strengthened our financial foundation, enabling continued investments and accelerated growth.
Our performance in FY 2024-25 reflects both 
the strength of the real estate sector and the strategic choices we’ve made over the past several years. We ended the year with our highest-ever annual booking value of ` 29,444 
Crores, growing 31% year-on-year on a strong base. This was supported by a 29% increase in booking volume to 25.73 Million sq. ft. Both GPL ’s booking value and booking volume were the highest ever recorded by any real estate developer in India.
Over the last three years, bookings have grown 
at a CAGR of 55%, with cumulative bookings of `64,203 Crores over this period. FY 2024-25 
also marked the eighth consecutive year of growth in booking value for the company, reaffirming our leadership position in the Indian residential real estate sector. 
Importantly, our growth was broad-based. 
NCR, MMR, and Bengaluru contributed `10,523 Crores, ` 8,034 Crores, and ` 5,089 
Crores respectively. Twelve different projects across Mumbai, Gurugram, Noida, Bengaluru, Pune, and Hyderabad each exceeded ` 1,000 
Crores in booking value. No single market contributed more than 36%, and our largest project accounted for just 13%, underscoring the strength of our diversified portfolio.We also achieved a record ` 17,047 Crores in 
customer collections, up 49% over last year, and ` 7,484 Crores in operating cash flow, 
up by 73% over last year - both the highest ever for an Indian real estate developer. We delivered 18.4 Million sq. ft. across markets, a growth of 47%. These outcomes reflect our ability to scale responsibly while remaining deeply focused on delivery.
On the back of this strong operating 
performance, we reported a 57% increase in total income to ` 6,848 Crores, a 65% rise 
in EBITDA to ` 1,970 Crores, and an increase 
of 93% in PAT to ` 1,400 Crores . Based on 
our FY 2024-25 booking performance, we expect over ` 7,700 Crores in EBIT and nearly 
`4,500 Crores in net profit to be recognised 
over the next 3–4 years as the projects that were sold this year are completed and achieve revenue recognition. 
This year, we also took a major step towards 
securing our long-term growth through a `6,000 Crores Qualified Institutional 
Placement (QIP), the largest QIP in Indian  real estate history. This reflects the strong conviction of investors in the Godrej brand and our strategic direction. The capital raised will allow us to significantly scale our project pipeline, expand into new geographies, and invest in long-term capabilities to build an even stronger, more future-ready GPL.
Our business development strategy remained 
disciplined and opportunity-driven.  In FY 2024-25, we added 14 new projects across Noida, Gurugram, MMR, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Pune, Ahmedabad, and Indore, with an estimated saleable area of 19 Million sq. ft. and a projected booking value of `26,450 Crores. This ensures a healthy 
launch pipeline and future visibility across growth markets.
In FY 2025-26, we aim to build on this 
momentum and cross ` 32,500 Crores in 
residential bookings—driven by a robust set of new launches and strong sustenance sales. With a healthy balance sheet, sectoral tailwinds, and operational momentum, we are confident of maintaining our growth trajectory.

Through our crop residue management initiative 
in Punjab, we transformed 97 villages, managed 17,368 hectares of farmland, and averted over 13,800 Tonnes of CO
2 emissions—driving

Health and safety remain central to our approach. 
Our Safety Management System, built on a proactive PDCA (plan–do–check–act) cycle, is ISO 45001:2018 certified across all project sites, supporting our ‘Score Zero’ aspiration for safety incidents.
Looking  Ahead
Our strategy continues to be focused on the pillars of scalable growth, disciplined execution, and stakeholder trust. The real estate sector provides tremendous long-term opportunity. Our strong balance sheet, diversified portfolio, and execution capabilities provide us the opportunity to continue to build on the momentum your business has generated over the past few years. Our ambition is not just to grow, but to do so with integrity, empathy, and purpose. 
On behalf of all of us at Godrej Properties, I would 
like to thank our customers, partners, investors, and shareholders for your continued support.  Your belief in our journey drives us every day.

Pirojsha Godrej  
Executive Chairperson
We were included in the S&P Global 2025 
Sustainability Yearbook, ranked among the top 10% of real estate companies globally, and named an Industry Mover.  We also continued to feature in the Dow Jones Emerging Markets Best in Class Index and secured a 5-star rating in GRESB for the fifth consecutive year.
Meaningful Impact on Communities
We are proud to have fully utilised our CSR funds in FY 2024-25. Through our BOCW programmes, we reached 32,500 construction workers, unlocking ` 88.38 Crores in government funds. 
Our solid waste management efforts diverted 53,239 Tonnes from landfills and recycled 99% of construction waste at source, making GPL a Net-zero waste organisation.At GPL, quality is a fundamental commitment.  Our dedicated 300-member quality team, reporting directly to the CEO, ensures unbiased assessments across all projects. We’ve institutionalised transparent, objective, and independent quality frameworks that set a new industry benchmark. This rigor in execution is central to the trust we have built with customers and partners alike. We recognise this is a continuous journey and are committed to ensuring quality remains on our top priority.
We continue to evolve our customer experience 
journey, focusing not just on homes, but on relationships built through empathy, clarity, and consistency. Our Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 67% is a testament to this approach. From thoughtful design to responsive service, we strive to create homes that feel personal and joyful at every stage of the journey.
Empowering People, Enabling Inclusion
We believe in empowering people—both within the company and across our value chain. Our learning academy, Alchemy, drives leadership development and capability-building at all levels. We are proud to be the first among Indian real estate companies to achieve 38.6% diversity representation, including 35.2% cis-women and 3.4% representation from LGBTQ+ individuals and persons with disabilities.
We also digitised worker engagement, scaled 
mental wellness programmes, and enabled longer-term participation from construction workers—ensuring our people practices are future-ready and inclusive.
Building a Greener Tomorrow
We recognise that our role as developers goes beyond building structures. It includes shaping sustainable, inclusive, and resilient communities. 
In FY 2024-25, we added five Net-zero Waste 
(Design) projects and one Net-zero Energy (Design) project to our portfolio. All our sites continue to be ISO 14001:2015 certified for Environmental Management, and sustainability targets are now embedded into senior leadership KPIs. 
Our near-term climate targets, validated by the 
Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), were an important milestone last year. This year, we submitted our commitment for a long-term Net-zero transition to SBTi. We continue to engage vendors through joint emission reduction plans and capability-building workshops. 
In FY 2025-26, we aim to

PERFORMANCE

PIPELINE

SUSTAINABILITY

• Our focus on sustainable 
development covers environmental & social parameters including site selection and planning, pedestrian friendly developments, indoor environmental quality, maximising day lighting and natural ventilation, water and energy efficiency and responsible material sourcing.
• Our near term emission reduction targets emission reduction targets are aligned with climate science standards and have been validated by SBTi.

GRI 2-22Q. How is Godrej Properties driving 
sustainability across its business operations?
Sustainability is embedded in everything we do—from 
project design to operations and workforce engagement. Our inclusion in the S&P Dow Jones Best in Class Indices is a recognition of this effort, but our motivation goes beyond rankings.
We have been successful in adding 6 IGBC Net 
Zero Waste (Design) and 1 IGBC Net Zero Energy (Design) project in our portfolio advancing our Net Zero commitment. 
We work closely with our supply chain to promote 
decarbonisation—conducting training workshops and encouraging the use of energy-efficient materials. On-site, we focus on worker safety, upskilling, and long-term career enablement.
We also see sustainability through the lens of inclusion. 
Our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) practices ensure opportunities for growth across backgrounds and roles—strengthening our social impact alongside environmental performance.
Q. What initiatives has Godrej Properties 
undertaken to strengthen customer trust and enhance their  experience?
Trust and experience are central to our value proposition. 
In FY 24-25, we reimagined home handovers into celebratory “Shubharambh” moments, with senior leadership participating to mark the occasion. This transformed handovers into a festive, deeply personal experience.
We launched Impressions, a social media series 
capturing authentic stories from our customers—building relatability and advocacy. Over 200 customer videos were published, enhancing community engagement. 
Technology remains a key enabler. Our Godrej Properties 
mobile app (4+ rating) provides real-time purchase and project updates. The app now supports alternate payment modes and has doubled digital collections.
Our WhatsApp-based service has also been upgraded 
to allow real-time audio/video support, improving responsiveness and transparency.
These initiatives together reflect our commitment to a 
relationship-driven, technology-enabled, and emotionally engaging customer journey.Q. Can you provide insights into how 
technological innovations have enhanced operational efficiency and supported the company’s growth ambitions?
We’ve made significant strides in integrating technology 
into core functions. Our in-house design tech vertical now leverages generative AI for architectural accuracy and efficiency. By collaborating with AI startups, we’ve strengthened design delivery and minimised deviation from blueprints.
In construction, our 3D-printed villa in Pune represents 
a leap forward—faster, sustainable, and highly precise. On the sales front, AI-driven analytics and personalised digital campaigns have enhanced outreach and conversion rates.
Beyond efficiency, our innovations aim to create real 
impact. Our labour productivity app ensures transparent incentives and financial access, helping our workforce grow alongside us. We believe technology must uplift—not just optimise.
Q. Looking ahead, what are the key priorities 
and strategies that will drive the next phase of growth for Godrej Properties?
As we move into our next phase, our priorities remain 
clear: scale responsibly, execute consistently, and grow profitably.
We will deepen our presence in core regions like NCR, 
MMR, Pune and Bengaluru while selectively entering tier-1 and tier-2 cities with strong demand dynamics. In FY 24-25, we entered Indore through two plotted development acquisitions—reflecting our calibrated approach to market entry.
We’re expanding across mid-income, premium, and 
luxury segments, and exploring lifestyle-led formats aligned with post-pandemic preferences. Sustainability will remain a core focus, with our Net Zero goals shaping design, construction, and operations.
Disciplined capital allocation, customer centricity, and 
operational excellence will continue to anchor our growth strategy. We are confident that our foundation is strong—and the future is full of opportunity.
Q. What has enabled Godrej Properties to 
achieve leadership in the real estate sector?
Our leadership has been built on three core pillars: 
execution, discipline, and foresight.
Between 2019 and 2021, our growth hovered around 
15%. In the last two years, however, we’ve scaled rapidly, growing booking value by 56% in FY 22-23, 84% in FY 23-24, and 31% in FY 24-25 on a much higher base. This acceleration is the result of proactive capital raises at strategic junctures in FY 18-19, FY 20-21, and again in FY 24-25 with the largest QIP ever seen in the sector.
Our financial agility, coupled with strong internal 
accruals, has allowed us to maintain a healthy balance sheet, reducing net gearing from 0.7x to ~0.2x. Equally important is our pan-India presence, which gives us operational flexibility and risk diversification across cycles.
The strength of the Godrej brand continues to be a key 
differentiator—enabling faster partnerships, smoother market entries, and stronger customer recall. Being part of the Godrej Industries Group enhances our market position, improves access to land, and lowers our cost of capital.
Q. The real estate sector is undergoing 
significant transformation. How is Godrej Properties navigating these changes?
The Indian real estate market is becoming increasingly 
segmented defined by varying demand drivers across regions and shifting buyer expectations. Post-COVID, we’ve seen a decisive shift: homeowners are now prioritising quality of life, larger spaces, and integrated amenities. To navigate this, we’ve doubled down on local empowerment. Our zonal leadership model allows for market-sensitive decision-making.
This is backed by professional management and data-led 
insights, enabling us to anticipate and act on consumer shifts quickly.
We continue to evolve with sustainability imperatives and 
customer-centric design innovations. With a responsive operating model, financial discipline, and strong brand trust, we are well-equipped to lead through the next 
phase of change.Gaurav Pandey
Managing Director and Chief Executive OfficerIN CONVERSATION  
WITH MD & CEO
We are the only developer with a truly 
pan India presence, which helps us balance risk while scaling efficiently. Our strategy of self-development gives us control over execution and margins critical in a sector where trust and delivery timelines matter deeply.

Resilience & Risk Management
Reporting and Monitoring
Risks are monitored regularly against 
tolerance levels. Material topics are reassessed annually with external assurance to ensure accuracy and relevance.Risk Identification
We identify key sustainability and value 
creation factors across our ventures, operations, and initiatives, by engaging external stakeholders and assessing financial performance, climate impact, and ESG exposures.OUR APPROACH
(as per GRI Universal Standards 2021)
GPL ensures reporting consistency with a standardised definition of 'material' across all reports. Our materiality matrix 
integrates internal and external criteria, prioritising climate change factors to support sector goals aligned with national commitments. Acknowledging the risks and opportunities linked to climate change, we align our assessments and disclosures with globally recognised frameworks like the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosure (TCFD), CDP, and the Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi).MATERIALITY 
Our materiality assessment and stakeholder engagement follow AA1000 principles—
Materiality, Completeness, and Responsiveness. The derived material themes are aligned with the GRI Universal Standards 2021. We  maintain reporting consistency by following a standardised definition of 'material' across all reports.
Analysing Materials and Prioritising 
Identified Concerns
We prioritise topics using the Double 
Materiality Principle, considering how the company affects the economy, society, and environment (Inside Out), and how external factors affect the company (Outside In).Implementation and Validation of Management
The Board and Senior Management review 
identified risks, approve outcomes, and integrate them into the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework through defined action plans.

ENGAGING LOCAL COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS
We conduct Environmental and Social Impact 
Assessments (ESIAs) at all project sites to evaluate potential effects on surrounding communities and ecosystems. These include localised stakeholder impact assessments to identify specific social, economic, and environmental concerns, forming the basis for targeted mitigation plans.
To foster transparency and trust, we have established 
clear and accessible communication channels with local stakeholders. These include structured community meetings, consultations, surveys, CSR initiatives, and awareness Programmes. Project-related information is shared proactively in a clear, timely, and culturally appropriate manner.
We actively encourage feedback through multiple 
contact points—such as email, helplines, and in-person interactions—outlined in our publicly available Stakeholder Engagement Policy.  To ensure meaningful participation, we support capacity-building initiatives that help local stakeholders effectively engage with the company.
We regularly conduct perception surveys and 
community reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of our engagement strategies and identify emerging issues. These are supplemented by direct meetings with community representatives to ensure concerns are promptly addressed.
All grievances are tracked through a formal mechanism 
that ensures timely resolution and continuous improvement. Our stakeholder engagement Programmes are applied consistently across all local operations, reinforcing our commitment to inclusive, responsible, and responsive development.
Understanding our stakeholders is critical 
to the long-term success of our business. Regular engagement with them helps to shape our strategy and ultimately informs our decisions so that we can deliver outstanding places and positive outcomes for all stakeholders.BUILDING SHARED FUTURES

INTEGRITY IN ACTION
Our Corporate Governance framework is designed 
to foster sustainable and transparent growth, while consistently generating economic value and safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders. We champion fair and transparent business practices through a well-structured corporate governance framework that not only guides ethical decision-making but also ensures active and inclusive engagement with all stakeholders.
The Board of Directors plays a central role in ensuring 
effective governance, overseeing the implementation of strategic decisions, and maintaining a culture of accountability across the organisation. By prioritising fairness in our interactions with regulators, employees, customers, vendors, investors, and the broader community, we reinforce our commitment to responsible corporate citizenship. 
As a publicly listed entity, GPL rigorously complies 
with the corporate governance norms prescribed by the National Stock Exchange of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), including the appointment of independent directors to its Board, further strengthening our dedication to oversight, transparency, and stakeholder trust.GPL COMMITTEES  
Eight board-led committees provide strategic oversight across critical focus areas, shaping corporate direction, ensuring effective implementation, and monitoring performance, risk, and policy adherence. The Board of Directors recognises that diversity is integral to long-term success, and currently comprises seven members with varied geographic origins, age groups, genders, ethnicities, cultural backgrounds, professional skills, and industry expertise, enhancing GPL ’s agility and competitiveness.
During the financial year, the Board met four times,

The Whistleblowing mechanism provides a platform where instances of code breaches, discrimination, harassment, or safety concerns can be reported anonymously. During the quarterly meetings of the Audit Committee, the Board of Directors is informed of every complaint.
A robust whistleblower mechanism is a cornerstone 
of ethical and transparent governance within any organisation. It fosters a culture of accountability and integrity by providing employees, stakeholders, and other parties with a secure and trustworthy avenue to report any unethical, illegal, or unsafe behaviour. The salient features of our whistleblowing mechanism are highlighted below:
• We have a dedicated Whistleblower Officer for 
managing whistleblower complaints.
• The whistleblowing mechanism provides a platform where instances of code violations, discrimination, harassment, or safety concerns can be reported.
• There are four ways of reaching out to the whistle blowing platform: telephone, Email, Web Portal and Chat bot. • The whistleblower platform is managed independently by a third party 
• The whistleblowing platform allows for anonymous submission of complaints. All complaints and identities of whistleblowers are handled with the utmost confidentiality, in accordance with the wishes of the complainant.
• The whistleblower policy has a strict zero-tolerance policy against any form of retaliation towards whistleblowers. Any form of discharge, threat, discrimination, or other adverse action against a whistleblower is strictly prohibited.
• To ensure effective utilisation of the whistleblower mechanism, regular training Programmes are conducted for all employees. These sessions cover the purpose of the mechanism, how to access the reporting platform, and the protections afforded to whistleblowers.
• The process for investigating reports is clearly defined within the whistleblower policy. Each report is assessed promptly, and investigations are carried out in an unbiased and systematic manner. Findings are documented, and appropriate corrective actions are taken based on the outcomes of each investigation.

RISK APPETITE
Risk appetite forms a foundational part of our risk management approach. It defines the level and type of risk we are willing to accept in pursuit of our strategic and operational objectives. For each identified risk, we assess its potential impact and likelihood, and evaluate it against our predefined appetite thresholds, ranging from zero to high tolerance.  Risk appetite levels are determined in alignment with business goals and are embedded into the annual risk assessment cycle, guiding the development of mitigation plans and influencing the review process by the Risk Management Committees. By integrating risk appetite into our governance framework, we ensure a balanced approach, encouraging innovation and growth while safeguarding organisational resilience.

CHAMPIONING 
CLIMATE POLICY THROUGH ADVOCACYOur approach to public policy engagement and 
climate advocacy is grounded in our commitment to sustainability and responsible corporate citizenship. Recognising the far-reaching implications of climate change for our business and communities, we actively support policies aligned with the Paris Agreement and a just transition to a low-carbon economy.
To ensure our lobbying efforts and trade association 
memberships reflect these objectives, we have instituted a structured, transparent governance framework that holds us accountable to both our climate goals and our stakeholders:
EXECUTIVE OVERSIGHT
Our public policy engagements are governed through a clearly defined framework with accountabilities extending to the relevant functional senior executive levels. The Managing Director & CEO plays a pivotal leadership role, including co-chairing the FICCI Committee on Urban Development and Real Estate, reinforcing our commitment at the strategic level.
POLICY POSITION STATEMENT
We have publicly articulated our support for the goals of the Paris Agreement, including limiting global warming to well below 2°C and pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. This position informs all our advocacy and policy engagement efforts.
MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
A centralised and robust management system is in place to oversee lobbying activities and trade association memberships. This system includes detailed documentation of our engagements, representatives, financial contributions, and alignment with business and sustainability objectives.MONITORING, REVIEW, AND 
ALIGNMENT PROCESSES
Our approach ensures transparency, consistency, and 
alignment with international climate goals through the following mechanisms:
Direct Lobbying Activities
All climate-related lobbying initiatives are reviewed regularly to ensure consistency with our climate strategy and the principles of the Paris Agreement. These activities are documented, monitored for effectiveness, and subject to internal oversight.
Trade Associations
We maintain a centralised database of all trade association memberships. This database includes information such as the purpose of the association, our representatives, membership costs, and the strategic value derived from participation. Regular reviews are conducted to evaluate continued alignment with our climate and business goals.
Misalignment Assessment and Response
We have established a clear framework to assess and address potential misalignments between the climate-related positions of trade associations and our own. Where discrepancies are identified, we engage constructively with the association to encourage alignment or consider withdrawing from the membership if alignment cannot be achieved.
Functional Oversight and Audit
Senior functional leaders are responsible for overseeing trade association memberships within their departments to ensure relevance and alignment with strategic objectives. In addition, our Internal Audit team conducts periodic reviews to verify compliance with internal policies and external regulatory requirements, ensuring transparency and ethical conduct.
TRANSPARENCY AND REPORTING
We are committed to transparent disclosure of our climate advocacy efforts. Our reporting includes details of our direct climate-related lobbying activities and positions and climate-related initiatives of the trade associations we are part of. We also continuously review how these engagements align with our climate policy.

We acknowledge climate-

ESG performance is now integrated into annual targets, procurement protocols, and executive remuneration frameworks, reinforcing our commitment to long-term value creation through responsible and climate-conscious decision-making.Progress towards net-zero targets depends not only on internal action but also on strong regulatory frameworks and collaborative partnerships. Recognising that a substantial share of our emissions lies beyond our direct operational control, we view government policies, industry standards, and evolving climate mandates as critical enablers in advancing our decarbonisation efforts.At the management level, we have taken key initiatives to drive accountability and align ESG with financial performance:
• Sustainability targets are now embedded 
within annual objectives, with corresponding compensation structures tied to their achievement across all roles, departments, and business functions.

Identifying Climate Related Risks & Opportunities
Building on our FY 2023 scenario analysis, we continue 
to assess both transition and physical climate risks, identifying potential challenges and opportunities for climate mitigation. We recognise that climate change is not confined to site operations alone—its impact extends across our entire value chain, influencing business resilience, supply chains, and stakeholder expectations.
To strengthen our commitment to climate resilience, 
we have embedded the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) framework into our management structure and risk assessment approach, ensuring a comprehensive and proactive response to climate-related challenges and opportunities.
Physical Climate-Related Risk Scenario Analysis
Climate change scenario analysis is a crucial tool for 
organisations to anticipate, evaluate, and manage climate-related risks and opportunities. It provides a structured approach to understanding potential future impacts, enabling businesses to develop resilient strategies—a key consideration for investors and stakeholders.
In line with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial 
Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations, we assess multiple climate scenarios, including one aligned with the 2015 Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C goal and a TO EVALUATE PHYSICAL CLIMATE RISKS, WE 
APPLIED TWO SHARED SOCIOECONOMIC PATHWAYS (SSP s)
SSP-1
(RCP-2.6), representing a low-emission, 
sustainable future
SSP-5
(RCP-8.5), depicting a high-emission, business-as-usual trajectorybusiness-as-usual (BAU) scenario, where physical risks such as flooding, heatwaves, and water scarcity pose significant challenges.
This assessment incorporated site-level surveys, peer 
reviews, and stakeholder consultations. Each identified risk was systematically analysed using a four-factor framework—likelihood, impact, vulnerability, and speed of onset—with additional considerations for adaptability and time sensitivity. Finally, risks were prioritised to focus on the most material climate-related threats, ensuring a proactive and strategic approach to climate resilience.
The assessment concentrated on locations that are 
particularly vulnerable to climate change impacts, including rising temperatures, changing precipitation patterns, water scarcity, and extreme climate hazards. Climate Risk Recognition and Context
Integrating Climate Risks into Enterprise 
Risk Management
Our approach to risk management encompasses the 
entire spectrum, from identifying and categorising risks to implementing effective mitigation strategies. We conduct sensitivity analysis and stress testing over time to bolster our readiness in handling risks. The Risk Management Committee is tasked with overseeing the company’s risk management function, ensuring adherence to established policies and procedures. To systematically identify and address risks, we have established an enterprise-wide Risk Management Framework through our Risk Management Charter. Following a comprehensive assessment of climate-related risks, we have integrated prioritised climate-related risks into GPL ’s Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework.
These include:
• Current Regulation
• Emerging Regulation
• Technology Risk
• Legal Risk
• Market Risk
• Reputational Risk
We identified key locations experiencing heightened 
vulnerability to the physical effects of climate change.
Transition Risk
We identify transition risks under both the Below 2°C and 
Net Zero Emissions (NZE) scenarios (orderly transition scenarios). While physical risks are relatively subdued in these pathways, transition risks are elevated due to stringent policies and rising stakeholder expectations.
In contrast, under a “business-as-usual” scenario, 
delayed climate action may keep transition risks low in the short term but significantly heightens physical risks, potentially causing severe disruptions.
The identified risks span reputational, regulatory, 
technological, and market-related categories. These have been classified based on their potential severity, ranging from low to high-medium risk, with corresponding opportunities also recognised.

How we Measure our Progress
Our climate-related goals are deeply integrated 
with our broader Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) commitments, which are embedded across all levels of the organisation—from leadership to operational teams.
To monitor our progress, we utilise comprehensive 
internal dashboards and ensure transparent public reporting, supported by third-party assurance.
As part of our commitment to sustainability, we 
have implemented a company-wide Occupational Health & Safety (OH&S) Management System and an Environmental Management System (EMS). The attainment of ISO certifications across our construction sites further reflects our dedication to climate resilience and environmental stewardship.
Godrej Properties operates as a water-positive and 
carbon-neutral organisation for Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. We remain focused on reducing emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 categories, while actively working to minimise waste generation throughout our operations.
To measure our progress against the commitments 
for climate risk management, we have set targets across decarbonisation (scope emission intensities), waste, water and certification of our green buildings.Our Climate Commitments
During the 2023-2024 fiscal year, we carried out 
a comprehensive risk assessment and scenario analysis pertaining to climate change, aligning with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) Framework. Throughout this reporting period, we have prioritised the management of climate change-related risks.
In accordance with the Paris Agreement, we have 
been active participants in the Science Based Target (SBT) initiative since 2020. Our approved targets seek to achieve a 72.6% reduction in scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions per square metre by the 2035 fiscal year.
Moving forward, we remain steadfast in our 
commitment to evaluating the financial implications of climate change on our business operations. During the upcoming Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) reporting cycle, we are committed to disclosing quantified impacts, encompassing both risks and opportunities, across a range of climate change scenarios. Furthermore, our enterprise risk management framework will systematically incorporate real-world climate change risks.
Read more about Environment Target and Progress at Pg. 44Managing Transition Risks Through  
Strategic Climate Action
As part of our climate strategy and in line with our 
commitment to mitigate transition risks associated with the shift to a low-carbon economy, we have established a structured Internal Carbon Pricing (ICP) mechanism. 
This is a strategic tool designed to align capital allocation, 
procurement, and operational decisions with our long-term Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi)-validated decarbonisation goals.
Following the Task Force on Climate-related Financial 
Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations and aligned with CDP's ICP objectives, our ICP accounts for all scopes of 
Strategic Objectives of Implementing Internal Carbon Pricing
Our ICP is designed to support multiple cross-functional climate and business objectives:
• Conduct cost-benefit analysis of low-carbon 
alternatives and technologies
• Drive energy efficiency in design, construction, and operations
• Incentivise low-carbon investments across the project lifecycle
• Embed climate-related considerations in business and investment decision-making
• Strengthen climate risk assessments by incorporating emissions costs into project planning
• Identify and capitalise on low-carbon opportunities, such as material innovation and green building certifications
• Inform and influence strategic and financial planning by integrating climate costs into budgeting• Navigate evolving carbon regulations and markets, including India’s upcoming domestic carbon market under the 2022 Energy Conservation Bill
• Reduce upstream emissions through climate-aligned sourcing and supplier Programmes
• Achieve climate targets and policies, including our SBTi-validated Scope 3 goals
• Set a carbon offset budget for unavoidable emissions
• Stress-test investments for carbon price resilience and long-term sustainability
• Supplier engagement strategies, aligned with our SBTi commitment
• Meet Stakeholder Expectations by demonstrating transparent and responsible climate actionGHG emissions: Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (indirect from purchased energy), and Scope 3 (value chain emissions). The ICP plays a critical role in reshaping our supply chain and material sourcing strategy.
Current ICP Structure 
We have implemented an implicit pricing model with a 
preliminary internal carbon price of ` 978 per metric tonne 
of CO
2e, designed to assess and influence the emissions 
intensity of investment and procurement decisions without immediate cash flow implications.
THE ROAD AHEAD
Our Internal Carbon Price is a dynamic tool that will continuously adapt to our sustainability 
roadmap, market developments, and regulatory shifts. By internalising the cost of carbon, we aim to drive systemic behaviouralthe resilience of our real estate portfolio in a rapidly transitioning global economy.

Prioritised Risks Mapped to Capitals

Significant rainfall can 
cause flooding, harming assets and disrupting work; materials and equipment damage raises replacement costs, impacting project budgets.Intense rainfall causes soil instability, erosion, and flooding, damaging construction sites.Heavy rainfall can create slippery conditions at construction sites, increasing the risk of slips, trips, and falls, thereby compromising worker safety.
Elevated temperatures and heatwaves increase energy costs and labour wages due to productivity loss, ultimately affecting project expenditure.High temperatures can disrupt ecosystems, impacting biodiversity, water sources, and habitats which can lead to reduced property value due to environmental degradation or increased operational costs for climate-resilient infrastructure.Heatwaves impact worker health and productivity, adversely affecting output.

2,708Planting Seeds of Change
In our pursuit of carbon neutrality, we have launched 
'Afforestation of Land' programmes across India. Collaborating with Nisarg, we implemented SALM project on farmlands and ensured 95% survival rate of plants planted in community land in Beed in previous FYs. The SALM and tree plantation project has sequestered approximately 47,948.8 tCO
2e through integrated climate-smart interventions. Key 
activities included improved crop varieties, kitchen gardens, biogas units, summer ploughing, mango agro-horticulture, and fodder cultivation. These practices enhanced soil carbon, biomass productivity, and long-term ecosystem sustainability.

UNITED FOR A LOW-CARBON FUTURE 
Managing Crop Residue 
Changing weather patterns have significantly disrupted 
cropping cycles, leading farmers in North India to resort to stubble burning due to delayed monsoons. This practice contributes substantially to air pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR).
Our Crop Residue Management (CRM) initiative aligns 
with the 2020 guidelines for CRM in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and the National Capital Territory of Delhi, as outlined by the Indian government. In FY 2024-25, 17,368 hectares of farmland were saved from stubble burning across 97 villages - an impressive increase from 4,966 hectares the year before. The harvested stubble was creatively reused: converted into biomass pellets, applied as soil mulch, and used as fuel in sugarcane processing plants. A notable shift began in FY 24-25 with the launch of the “Jalana Nahin, Galana Hai” initiative, promoting composting over burning. 
This marks a major stride toward environmental 
sustainability and improved soil health. With continued commitment, skill development, and collaborative efforts, this forward-thinking strategy could redefine how paddy stubble is viewed and handled, transforming a persistent problem into a sustainable development opportunity. Also, to scale up this initiative, Godrej properties in collaboration with Feedback Foundation and with the support of the Agriculture Department, are establishing a Crop Residue Management Park at Village Bhagwanpur, Gurdaspur. Spanning 10 acres, this park will serve as a demonstration and learning site for composting practices using paddy stubble.

ENERGY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (E nMS)
As a real estate developer committed to a low-carbon future, our Energy Management System (EnMS) is central to 
improving operational sustainability and energy efficiency. While our direct energy footprint is limited, consumption does occur across regional, marketing, and sales offices at our project sites. Our energy management efforts are therefore directed at optimising use in these locations, in alignment with our broader climate goals.
To drive continuous improvement in our energy performance and efficiency, we align with global standards such as the 
Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC) and the Energy Performance Index (EPI) defined by ASHRAE (American Society of Heating, Refrigerating, and Air-Conditioning Engineers). All our projects are designed in compliance with these standards. Furthermore, all new projects within the reporting boundary are planned to incorporate on-site renewable energy generation through solar power.ENERGY AUDITS FOR

FROM DRYLANDS TO LIFELINES
Water scarcity remains one of the most urgent 
challenges of our time. We recognised the need for proactive, community-focused solutions and launched an integrated watershed development project in 2016. Spanning approximately 3,300 hectares, the initiative covered the villages of Bavi, Zapewadi, and Jamb in Maharashtra’s drought-prone Beed district.
The implementation phase was successfully completed 
in 2019, made possible through the invaluable support of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and our NGO partner. To assess the real, on-ground impact of the intervention, we collaborated with the Ekonnect Knowledge Foundation for an independent evaluation.POND REJUVENATION AT GODREJ 
SUNRISE ESTATE, CHENNAI
We undertook the transformation of a long-neglected 
pond into a thriving rainwater harvesting system.  This initiative went beyond infrastructure; it revitalised a forgotten space to serve both environmental and community needs.
An advanced stormwater drainage network was installed 
to capture and reuse rainwater, helping mitigate flood risk and support groundwater recharge. Around the rejuvenated pond, we developed a tranquil community park that offers green open spaces for recreation and wellness. Thoughtfully integrated landscaping and water features further reduced the urban heat island effect, creating a more pleasant and sustainable microclimate for residents.REPLENISH AND REUSE: WATER FOR THE LONG RUN
Harnessing Natural Topography for Sustainable Water Management
Designed to hold up to 4 Million litres of water, the retention pond is lined with a durable HDPE geomembrane. Weep holes on the upstream side allow gradual percolation into a separate storage tank, helping extend water availability into the post-monsoon months of September and October. This system significantly reduces dependence on external water sources such as tankers, thereby promoting sustainability and improving operational efficiency.  Climate change is steadily impacting groundwater availability for everyday use. To address this growing concern, we are adopting climate-resilient water management solutions within our communities. One such initiative is the development of water retention ponds - engineered to capture and store rainwater while preserving the site's natural contours. Through such thoughtful design, we are creating communities that are better equipped to manage water sustainably and live in greater harmony with nature. 
At Godrej City in Panvel, Maharashtra, we have utilised 
the site's natural topography to develop a sustainable and efficient water management system. With an average monsoon rainfall of around 450 mm per month, we constructed a strategically located water retention pond at an intermediate elevation, aligning with the natural contours and slopes of the land. Covering a catchment area of approximately 22 acres, the pond captures and stores rainwater, which is then distributed downstream using gravity flow.

GRI 2-25RESTORING WHILE WE BUILD
Environmental Impact Assessments are undertaken 
at every site in accordance with Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change (MoEFCC) regulations.
We refrain  from operational activities in notified 
areas, eco-sensitive zones, World Heritage sites, and IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) Category I-IV protected areas.     
We have taken meaningful steps toward achieving 
a net positive impact on biodiversity by going beyond mitigation to ensuring that the natural environment is left in a better state than before development. Our projects are designed to integrate sustainable amenities, including rainwater harvesting systems, solar panels, and other eco-friendly initiatives that actively reduce carbon emissions while promoting a healthier living environment. We are committed to conserving 15% to 20% of the natural topography across all developments. This year, we strengthened our biodiversity efforts by planting 6,227 trees across operational regions.
We are committed to achieving a net positive 
impact (NPI) on biodiversity by 2035 and “No Net Deforestation” by 2030 across all operations. 
Our Structured Approach to Mitigating Environmental Impact
1. AVOIDANCE
• Operations, construction, and development activities are 
strictly prohibited in legally protected areas, including IUCN-designated categories Ia, Ib, II, III, and IV.
• Technical standards have been established to incorporate biodiversity and ecosystem management into decision-making processes for both new and existing projects.
• Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are implemented to prevent the introduction of invasive species during transportation of vehicles and goods.
2. MINIMISATION
• Environmental Management Plans (EMPs) are employed to mitigate air, noise, water, and soil pollution.
• Greenbelt development initiatives are undertaken to reduce the impact of pollutants.
• Compliance with Biodiversity Management Plans is regularly reviewed across all project sites.
3. RESTORATION
• Restoration efforts focus on replanting native and endangered flora, removing invasive species, rehabilitating disturbed areas, and restoring water bodies to conserve biodiversity.4. OFFSETTING
• Initiatives include enhancing vegetation on barren lands and establishing medicinal plantations in community spaces, with active engagement of local communities.
• Planting native species is prioritised to foster ecological restoration.
5. TRANSFORMATION
• Conservation activities include protecting endangered species, setting up conservation centres, offering wildlife rescue services, and supporting forest fire prevention measures.
• Local community involvement is promoted through livelihood improvement initiatives, public awareness campaigns, and training for forest personnel.
• Sustainable practices are encouraged through the use of eco-certified wood.BIODIVERSITY RISK ASSESSMENTS Biodiversity Risk Assessment Process
DEFINE SCOPE
Identify project sites, adjacent areas 
(within 5-10 km), and relevant upstream/downstream activities.
IDENTIFY DEPENDENCIES AND IMPACTS
Assess how operations rely on and affect natural ecosystems (e.g., water use, habitat disruption).
SCREEN SENSITIVE AREAS
Use tools like IBAT, WWF Risk Filter, and ENCORE to map biodiversity risks at specific locations. - to be checked.
CLASSIFY RISKS
Categorise risks as physical, regulatory, reputational, or operational and integrated in the the organisation risk management framework.
CONSULT STAKEHOLDERS
Engage local communities, biodiversity experts, and regulators for validation and input.
INTEGRATE AND ACT
Feed results into risk management; prepare mitigation plans and implement site-level actions.
MONITOR AND REPORT
Track biodiversity KPIs, apply mitigation hierarchy, and disclose performance.
We prioritise the identification and monitoring of protected areas surrounding our project sites to evaluate and minimise our impact on them. We recognise biodiversity as a critical component of sustainable development. Our Biodiversity Risk Assessment Process is designed to systematically identify, evaluate, and manage nature-related risks across our operations and value chain. 
We follow a structured, location-specific approach to 
assess biodiversity risks, focusing on how our own operations, adjacent areas and value chain interact with nature. This means assessing dependencies (e.g., water regulation, flood protection, air purification) and impacts (e.g., habitat disruption, pollution, land use change) at specific project sites and along the upstream and downstream segments of our operations.
Our biodiversity risk assessment process is guided by 
globally recognised methodologies and frameworks like the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) LEAP approach, to ensure consistency, reliability, and transparency in identifying and managing nature-related risks.
Tree plantation at Godrej Hillview EstateA structured mitigation approach is followed, emphasising avoidance, minimisation, restoration, and offsetting to reduce environmental impact. 
 In FY 24-25, we carried out comprehensive 
biodiversity surveys at Maanhinjewadi in Pune, Sumthana in Nagpur, Sector 49 in Gurgaon, Banerghatta and Whitefield in Bengaluru to gain deeper insights into the local ecosystem, including flora, fauna, and ecological dynamics. Specialised stream surveys were conducted to document native topography, enabling us to align our development activities with the goal of minimising habitat disturbance. The primary biodiversity risks identified from the above assessments include habitat degradation and vegetation loss from land-use changes, soil degradation and erosion due to construction, air pollution, elevated noise levels; and introduction of invasive species threatening native biodiversity. We have devised comprehensive mitigation measures such as afforestation, native species restoration, pollution control, rainwater harvesting, installation of sewage treatment plants, and creating green buffers to safeguard local ecosystems. These surveys are being extended to all our development sites.

GRI 3-3UTILISATION OF SUSTAINABLE 
MATERIALS
We use building materials certified by GreenPro, an 
ecolabel developed by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). GreenPro follows a life cycle-based holistic assessment to evaluate products, ensuring they deliver measurable environmental benefits throughout their use.
The GreenPro ecolabel is accredited by the Global 
Ecolabelling Network (GEN) under GENICES—the internationally coordinated ecolabelling system that upholds the credibility of Type I Ecolabels in accordance with ISO 14024 standards. GreenPro is also aligned with the UN Environment's Guidelines for Providing Product Sustainability Information.
To earn GreenPro certification, products are 
evaluated across the following areas
• Product Design
• Product Performance
• Raw Material and Manufacturing Process
• Waste Management
• Life Cycle Assessment
• Product Stewardship
• Innovation
GreenPro-certified materials significantly enhance the 
performance of green buildings by reducing resource consumption and promoting occupant health and  
well-being.
These eco-labelled products support sustainable 
building practices in key areas such as:
• Energy Efficiency
• Indoor Environmental Quality (low-emitting VOC 
materials, toxic-free substances)
• Materials and Resources (low embodied carbon, recycled content)
• Water Management
• Waste Management (easily recyclable products)
• Sustainable SoilsGreenPro-certified products span a 
wide range of categories:
The Environmental Product Declarations 
(EPDs) and Health Product Declarations (HPDs) for some of these materials are provided on page no. 510. Some of the categories used by us are:

We have embedded the overall water management strategy into the design of our built environment, where we 
prioritise features that reduce water consumption for occupants. This includes the use of indigenous, drought-resistant vegetation, installation of low-flow water fixtures, and customer education initiatives to promote mindful water use.
Key Aspects Of Our Water Management Strategy
Engage With Customers
Spread awareness regarding the significance 
of water preservation and its environmental ramifications. Share practical guidance on implementing water-saving practices within individual properties. Collaborate with community-based organisations or initiatives focused on water conservation to host educational workshops, initiatives, or gatherings. Such endeavours foster a sense of community engagement, motivating customers to actively engage in conserving water resources.Encourage Design Of Water Efficient Homes
Create water-efficient design standards 
and checklists offering precise guidance for architects and facilities management teams. These resources should encompass details on water-saving fixtures, appliances, landscaping methods, and rainwater harvesting tactics.
Reduce Irrigation Water Requirements
Utilise indigenous flora and vegetation that 
are naturally suited to the regional climate and demand less water. Resilient species that are drought-tolerant can flourish with minimal irrigation, leading to a decrease in overall water consumption. Implement water-efficient irrigation methods like drip irrigation or micro-sprinklers. These systems deliver water precisely to the plant roots, minimising evaporation and ensuring effective water distribution.Enhance Awareness
Promote awareness by highlighting the 
importance of water efficiency, especially in residential developments recognised with the IGBC Platinum rating. Encourage individual water metering and emphasise the benefits of water-efficient design, such as reduced water bills, environmental sustainability, and long-term cost savings.
Minimise Dependence On Groundwater
Incorporate water-saving fixtures like low-
flow faucets, toilets, and shower-heads into all structures. Introduce rainwater harvesting systems to gather and store rainwater for non-potable purposes such as irrigation, toilet flushing, and cleaning.Measure Water Consumed
Implement water monitoring systems 
equipped with sensors to monitor water flow and usage across different sections of the property. Such systems offer valuable insights into specific areas exhibiting high or excessive water consumption.Responsible Consumption of Materials (Tonnes)

RAISING THE BAR IN QUALITY 
AND CRAFTSMANSHIP
Quality-Driven Procurement
We implement rigorous sourcing criteria to ensure 
that only the highest-quality raw materials are used. Our procurement process includes strict quality filters to assess materials, contractors, and construction techniques, ensuring compliance with industry best practices and project specifications at both the pre-construction and post-construction stages.
Training and Skill Development
A commitment to continuous learning drives our approach to manufacturing excellence. All stakeholders—contractors, design consultants, and project teams—undergo regular training to stay ahead of industry advancements, evolving construction techniques, and quality standards. By fostering a culture of collaborative learning, we enhance on-site efficiency and execution, ensuring our developments set new benchmarks in quality.
Performance Measurement through Quality 
Indexing
We are transitioning from subjective assessments 
to data-driven quality evaluation through the Quality Score Index (QSI)—one of the most advanced quality benchmarks in the industry. Assessed at every stage, from excavation to handover, QSI enables real-time evaluation of material quality, workmanship, and project execution, reinforcing our commitment to precision and reliability.Our strong system processes have been built around quality management. We have created a framework consisting of checklist for delivering the best quality in the industry. 
Engineering Excellence Through Critical to 
Quality (CTQ) Parameters
At GPL, quality is integral to every project stage, 
from design to delivery. Our Critical to Quality (CTQ) framework ensures key quality factors are met throughout.
End-to-End CTQ Framework
Product CTQs (Customer Delivery): We ensure zero structural defects in Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC), like beam sagging, concrete spalling, or structural cracks.
Design CTQs (Design Compliance): All structural 
elements adhere to IS codes, and building designs account for live, wind, and seismic loads per relevant IS standards.
Process CTQs (Execution Excellence): We follow correct 
curing processes, maintain adequate reinforcement cover, strictly adhere to structural grid distances, observe de-shuttering timelines, test concrete water for permissible chloride levels, and keep RCC line and level within acceptable tolerance limits.
Triple-Check Quality Mechanism
To support our CTQ framework, we use a three-tiered quality assurance model:
• Quality at Source | Compliance.
• Quality Culture | Leadership Walkthroughs
• Quality Delivery | Internal & External Audit
By systematically embedding CTQs and upholding our 
triple-check mechanism, GPL continues to raise the bar for structural integrity, design compliance, and flawless execution. This in-house digital quality app serves 4000+ users across 75 projects. It replaced paperwork, ensuring traceability and accountability. Get data-driven insights and full customisation with this system-driven solution, compliance, and flawless execution.
PROMOTING 
SUSTAINABLE LIFESTYLES
Recognising the immense potential for resource 
conservation in multi-dwelling residential communities, the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) introduced the IGBC Green Residential Societies Rating System. This initiative serves as a structured framework to help residential complexes monitor, manage, and reduce their consumption of natural resources. By adopting this system, residents can benefit from enhanced efficiency, lower utility costs, improved environmental impact, and a healthier community lifestyle, ensuring both tangible and intangible long-term advantages. Our mandate is to ensure a minimum of IGBC silver rating (or equivalent in other rating systems) across all projects.
STEPS TAKEN TOWARDS SUSTAINABLE 
& INCLUSIVE LIVING
• We promote sustainable transportation with 
pedestrian-friendly layouts to reduce fossil fuel reliance.
• We ensure buildings are within a 10-minute walk of transportation hubs.
• We implement energy efficiency schemes to lower energy bills and adopt low-maintenance design practices for all projects.
• Safety considerations are systematically integrated into the design and development of projects, encompassing key areas such as fire safety, structural integrity, and electrical and gas safety.
• The resilience of the built environment to both current and future natural disasters—particularly flooding—is a core consideration during the design and development stages. Detailed flood risk assessments are conducted early in the planning process to inform critical design decisions. These include elevating plinth levels above known flood lines, incorporating efficient stormwater drainage systems, and using permeable surface materials to enhance ground absorption and reduce runoff.
• We maintain clear evacuation plans and conduct training for tenants and visitors during handover.
• GPL generates skill development opportunities for the local communities through traineeships.• Our CSR programmes are thoughtfully designed to educate and engage local communities by raising awareness of key social and environmental challenges.
• In collaboration with NGO partners, we enhance public spaces to improve liveability and foster community well-being. Through initiatives focused on biodiversity, waste management, and other environmental improvements, these programmes transform open, accessible areas into vibrant, sustainable spaces that encourage social interaction and a stronger sense of community.
• We actively promote local economic development by sourcing goods and services from local SMEs, strengthening regional supply chains, and supporting the creation of local jobs and entrepreneurial growth.
• GPL is committed to creating inclusive environments that go beyond compliance with accessibility laws by integrating universal design principles into every aspect of our developments. Our spaces are thoughtfully designed to accommodate individuals of all abilities, featuring ramps, elevators, accessible restrooms, designated parking for persons with disabilities, and non-slip surfaces.
• GPL conducts ESIAs around project sites to evaluate potential effects on local communities and ecosystems. Based on these insights, we implement mitigation plans to minimise negative impacts and ensure our developments are both environmentally responsible and socially inclusive

ADVANCED WASTEWATER TREATMENT TECHNOLOGY
At Godrej City, we have implemented an Upflow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket (UASB) system integrated with a trickling 
filter Sewage Treatment Plant (STP). This advanced wastewater treatment technology enhances efficiency, lowers operational costs, and minimises environmental impact.
SMART WATER METERS
Smart water meters track real-time usage and detect leaks, helping reduce wastage. Over 18 months, this led to a saving of approximately 42.3 Lakhs Litres of drinking water.
WIRELESS CCTV
The deployment of wireless CCTV systems has enhanced security while significantly reducing environmental impact. By eliminating the need for extensive cabling, this technology has lowered installation and maintenance costs, improved image clarity over time, and ensured faster repairs. Additionally, its energy-efficient design contributes to a lower carbon footprint, providing a durable, long-term security solution with a lifespan of up to a decade. 
SOLAR PANELS
We have adopted a hybrid energy strategy across our offices and project sites in the West-East Zone, combining conventional sources with solar photovoltaic and wind energy. Supported by green power partnerships, this approach reduces reliance on fossil fuels and strengthens our commitment to sustainable operations. At our projects in Pune and Mumbai, solar systems have generated 8,12,042 kWh of clean energy, resulting in electricity savings of approximately I1.43 Crores and a reduction of 624 tCO
2 emissions as of FY 2024–25.INNOVATION IN ACTION
Innovation drives how we build smarter, faster, and more sustainably. From pioneering India’s first 
3D-printed villa to integrating renewable energy, smart water meters, and advanced wastewater treatment technologies, we’re reimagining every aspect of urban living. Our developments also feature wireless surveillance and intelligent building systems that enhance safety and efficiency. With each breakthrough, we move closer to creating homes that are future-ready, resource-conscious, and truly differentiated.
INDIA’S FIRST 3D-PRINTED VILLA  BY 
GODREJ PROPERTIES
GPL has unveiled India's first 3D-printed ground-plus-one (G+1) villa at Godrej Eden Estate in 
Pune, marking a significant advancement in innovation and sustainable construction. Completed in just four months, this innovative project showcases the potential of additive manufacturing to revolutionise the real estate sector. By employing 3D printing technology, GPL has significantly reduced construction time, material waste, and labour costs, while enhancing precision and durability. 
This approach not only minimises the environmental footprint but also aligns with GPL 's focus 
on pioneering eco-friendly building practices. The villa's design incorporates energy-efficient features and utilises sustainable materials, setting new benchmarks for green real estate development in India.

Performance Appraisal Framework
Our performance appraisal framework is designed to support holistic development, encourage 
accountability, and align individual efforts with organisational goals.
Goal Setting 
At the beginning of each review cycle, employees define their annual goals in collaboration with their managers. These goals are aligned with business priorities using the Management by Objectives approach, ensuring clarity of expectations and strategic alignment.
Structured and Ongoing Reviews
We conduct two formal reviews — mid-year and annual — which assess progress, identify development areas, and reinforce accountability. These are based on clearly defined, measurable outcomes aligned with individual and team objectives, as well as the Godrej Capability Factors (GCFs) — a framework encompassing three key areas: Leading Self, Leading Others, and Leading Business.
Team based performance appraisal
Recognising that success is a collective endeavour, GPL uses a Business Index to capture and reward team performance. This index affects the variable compensation framework, reinforcing the value of collaboration, shared ownership, and mutual accountability.Agile ConversationsIn addition to formal reviews, we promote continuous feedback through agile conversations — real-time, informal check-ins between managers and team members. These ongoing dialogues enhance coaching, improve responsiveness, and build trust.
Multidimensional Feedback (360-Degree 
Appraisals)
For mid and senior-level employees, the appraisal 
process incorporates 360-degree feedback, providing a well-rounded view of individual performance and leadership effectiveness. Feedback is collected from peers, managers, team members, and in some cases, clients — ensuring a comprehensive assessment.

Laying the Foundation for Disability Inclusion
Our journey towards disability inclusion has matured from intention to infrastructure. Over the past two years, we have moved decisively from awareness to action—grounded in strategy, role-level fitment, and inclusive design. At the centre of this evolution is Project Pathmaker, a pioneering initiative to embed accessibility into workforce planning.
In partnership with Enable India, we undertook a 
deep-dive diagnostic of ten critical roles across Finance, Operations, Customer Centricity, and Sales & Marketing. Each role was evaluated using a Red-Amber-Green (RAG) framework to assess task suitability across physical, sensory and cognitive disabilities—pinpointing fully accessible roles, those requiring reasonable adjustments, and others that could be adapted through job carving.
This role-specific lens allows us to go beyond generalised 
inclusion and align hiring practices with business needs—building meaningful pathways for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).

PAY EQUITY
We are actively addressing the gender pay gap through a structured, three-pronged approach. In FY 2023-24, 
our unadjusted gender pay index stood at 66%, a figure shaped primarily by underrepresentation in senior roles. However, when adjusted for level and role, parity improves substantially 85% at entry level and 94% at senior level.
To close the remaining gap, we introduced correctional hikes as part of the April 2025 compensation cycle. 
High-performing employees are expected to reach parity within one year, while others will reach parity within two to three years. We also reviewed all incoming offers to ensure alignment with market benchmarks, thereby reducing the possibility of perpetuating inherited inequities.
Recognising that representation is inseparable from parity, we are investing in greater visibility of women 
in leadership. This includes strengthening return-to-work and caregiving policies to support women during life transitions.

We understand that flexible working conditions are key 
to ensuring a sustainable work-life balance. Our policies are designed to give employees control over their time and workstyle:
Flexible Scheduling
We operate on a core-hours model (10 AM – 4 PM), 
allowing all employees the freedom to structure their 42.5-hour work week around their personal preferences and responsibilities.
Remote and Hybrid Working Model
We are committed to fostering a flexible and empowering 
work environment for all our employees. Our hybrid work model encourages team collaboration while also supporting individual productivity and well-being. We have a Work from Home (WFH) policy that allows employees to work remotely for a few days each month. This policy is designed to provide flexibility and can be further adapted based on individual needs through consultation with their managers.
Part-Time Working Options
We offer adaptable part-time work structures, including 
3-day and 4-day work weeks, or reduced daily hours, empowering employees to choose what suits them best.Flexibility at Work
Leave Management
We understand that rest and recovery are essential to 
maintaining long-term employee health and productivity. To support this, we actively encourage our employees to utilise their annual leave through regular communications focused on promoting physical and mental rejuvenation. Our leave policy is designed with empathy and trust at its core. It includes a comprehensive array of options, such as a trust-based sick leave system that allows employees to take necessary health-related time off without affecting their privilege leave balance. This approach reflects our commitment to a caring and supportive workplace culture. Furthermore, employees receive full access to their entitled leave at the start of each calendar year, enabling them to plan their time off thoughtfully, balancing personal priorities with professional commitments. 
As per our policy, employees are provided with a 
minimum notice period of 2 months for Level 1, and 3 months for Levels 2, 3, and 4, prior to any significant operational changes that may affect them.
We are committed to fostering a workplace where employees’ mental, physical, and emotional wellbeing is 
prioritised. Through our comprehensive Employee Wellness Programme, we provide the necessary resources to support the holistic health of our workforce, ensuring they are equipped to succeed both professionally and personally.
Mental Health and Stress Management
Our partnership with Amaha, a leading mental health platform, offers 24/7 confidential access to licensed mental 
health professionals through our Employee Assistance Programme. Weekly "Mindful Mondays" sessions promote mindfulness, creativity, and personal growth. Our "Harmony Hours" policy reinforces mental boundaries by discouraging non-urgent emails between 8 PM and 8 AM.
Physical Health and Wellness Programmes

with professional instructors and access to a dedicated nutritionist. Operational Projects CoveredTraining and Awareness Initiatives
We've developed comprehensive programmes designed 
to educate and promote occupational health and safety among our employees. These initiatives encompass training sessions, motivational events, and health camps. Additionally, we consistently organise blood donation drives, health lectures, and safety campaigns. Our facilities also actively participate in significant events such as National Safety Day, Road Safety Week, and National Fire Service Day to further raise safety awareness and cultivate a culture of vigilance and preparedness.
Our Objective is to Provide a Safe work environment for 
all staff and workers, relying on four key elements of OHS risk management.Continual ImprovementTo proactively uphold safety standards, GPL utilises a rigorous internal audit process. This process evaluates site safety performance, pinpoints opportunities for enhancement, and ensures site teams implement corrective actions to drive continuous improvement.
Safety Infrastructure
We prioritise safety by ensuring every location has access to critical amenities: safety induction facilities for all personnel, on-site medical support including a nurse and ambulance services, established hospital partnerships, and comprehensive safety resources such as Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and certified electrical equipment.
OHS Management Systems
Our OHS Management System is designed to guarantee the implementation and effectiveness of safety measures. This is achieved through on-site execution supported by detailed Site Safety Plans, comprehensive Hazard Identification and Risk Assessments, a rigorous Work Permit System, and regular internal safety audits to assess performance.
People and Leadership

Our Comprehensive Approach to Safety
Ensuring the health, safety, and well-being of our workforce is a fundamental priority and a shared responsibility across all levels of the organisation. Our OH&S Management System is built on clearly defined procedures that are fully aligned with our Health & Safety Policy, ensuring consistent implementation across all project sites, corporate offices, and construction activities.
Senior management plays a pivotal role in driving our

To institutionalise safety performance, quantitative Key

Additionally, we have introduced a prioritisation and

Through this structured and data-driven approach, we
